messages:
Alex: Quick sync — Horizon reported intermittent customer isolation after a VPC peering update around 03:10 UTC. Seeing some pods lose access to on-prem services intermittently. Opening thread to track follow-ups and owners.
Jasmin: Thanks Alex. Do we have a root cause hypothesis yet?
Samir: Initial traces show dropped TCP sessions between peered subnets. Could be MTU or a route flap during the peering swap.
Lia (oncall): I captured packet drops from the on-prem edge: lots of fragmented packets, then conn reset. MTU mismatch is suspicious.
Alex: Can infra run a quick validation checklist? 1) confirm MTU across VPN/peering 2) check BGP hold timers/route churn 3) firewall NAT translations on the edge appliance.
infra-bot: Automated check kicked: bridgeproof check + peering-health scan started (job id: bp-2276). Will post results.
Jasmin: Assigning ownership: Samir for MTU validation and config fix, Lia to coordinate logs with customer, Alex to own rollout plan for fix and canary. Timeline: aim for remediation by EOD tomorrow.
Samir: On it. First step: run MTU probe from peered subnet to on-prem jumper. Command: ```ping -M do -s 1472 10.20.30.1``` If fragmentation, lower MSS/MTU or enable TCP MSS clamping on peering.
Lia (oncall): I've asked customer to run same probe from their edge and share results. Also asked for syslogs during 03:00-03:30 UTC window.
Alex: Also add an automated log alert: detect >5% fragmented packets across peering in 15m window. Put alert in prod-console under peering -> fragmentation.
Samir: If MTU isn't the issue, next suspect is transient route flapping from on-prem BGP dampening. I'll collect BGP update frequency and share.
infra-bot: bridgeproof results: MTU mismatch detected on on-prem edge (reported 1500 vs 1420 on AWS peering). Packet fragmentation rate: 6.7% in last 1h.
Jasmin: Good catch infra-bot. Samir — start small mitigation: enable MSS clamp at 1400 on peering node and monitor. Lia — coordinate customer maintenance window to apply on their edge if needed.
Samir: Rolling config to canary peering node now. Will tag change with rollback and diff in PR: ```git commit -m "mss-clamp: set 1400 on peering"``` PR: https://git.redwood/infra/peering/merge/1420
Lia (oncall): Customer confirmed they'll be available for 30m window tomorrow 01:00-01:30 PDT to accept edge change.
Alex: Postmortem action items (concrete):
- Samir: Validate MTU across all live peerings and enable MSS clamp where needed (owner: Samir, due: 2276620000).
- Lia: Collect on-prem syslogs and confirm customer edge config after change (owner: Lia, due: 2276580000).
- Jasmin: Add fragmentation alert and dashboard card, link to incident runbook (owner: Jasmin, due: 2276570000).
- Alex: Run a one-week cadence to scan for recurring fragmentation patterns and add to weekly incident trends (owner: Alex, due: 2277200000).
All: Please ack when you have tasks assigned.
Samir: Acked. Started the canary roll now. Monitoring latency & tcp retransmits.
Lia (oncall): Acked. I will post logs once customer confirms.
Jasmin: Acked. I'll create alert + dashboard and ping here when done.
infra-bot: Canary deployment succeeded on node peering-3. Fragmentation dropped to 0.4% in 10m window.
Alex: Nice. Keep monitoring for 24h. We'll close this thread once all action items have timestamps and owners confirmed.
Samir: Logging follow-ups in the remediation tracker: https://trello.redwood/incidents/horizon-peering-2276543210
Jasmin: Added runbook link and alert docs to the tracker.
Lia (oncall): Customer confirmed edge patch completed. No further isolations reported in last 2 hours.
Alex: Thanks team. Filing postmortem follow-up with owners. We'll revisit in next weekly incident trends to see if this pattern recurs. :thumbsup:
text_summary: Horizon customer experienced intermittent isolation after VPC peering update. MTU mismatch found causing fragmentation; MSS clamp applied as canary, fragmentation dropped. Action items assigned to Samir, Lia, Jasmin, Alex with due timestamps. Monitoring and follow-ups planned.
